## Bucket 4 — improvements (2) · fix-now · needs judgment (/framework-audit-fix)

- **D5-token-audit-two-copies** · `D5` · _open_ — RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17: confirmed and WIDENING. Shipped plugin/commands/token-audit.md 1715w vs forge-local .claude/commands/token-audit.md 2309w; shipped still carries an old `## Never` while the forge-local gained `## Domain separation` + `## Do this`, and forge-local advanced again in f727444 (the jq stub gate) while shipped last moved in 51b9adf. The drift is STRUCTURAL, not accidental: the forge-local copy is the one that actually runs during an audit, so it gets improved; the shipped copy is only ever touched incidentally. DECISIVE EVIDENCE the row previously missed — the shipped copy is not merely stale, it is HARMFUL: it points the agent at `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/library/token-audits/LEDGER.md` (line 30), a CORE-TRACKED file that ships to every install, so a bound project running /token-audit appends ITS session findings into the framework's shipped library (D2 contamination by construction). It also lacks the entire `npm run token-history` / history.json half, which is forge-local anyway — so a project can only half-run the loop. RECOMMEND: delete the shipped copy; the token audit is a forge-local practice with a forge-local CLI and store. Alternative if it must ship: repoint its ledger at a PROJECT-local path and generate it from the forge-local source.
  - _pattern:_ a command SHIPS only if its whole loop ships — a port that loses its CLI and writes into the shipped library is worse than not shipping it.
- **D8-qa-pass-not-bound-to-sha** · `D8` · _open_ — The webapp pack's commit gate verifies a STICKER, not the artifact. commit-gate.sh:35-44 reads `gh issue view <N> --json labels` and allows the commit when qa:pass + review:pass are present — there is NO SHA anywhere in the hook, so the pass is bound to the ISSUE, never to the code being committed. Run /qa green at SHA A, then make three more commits citing (#N): every one is allowed and none is re-verified, so the guarantee decays with each commit. tester.md:70-72 closes the loop the wrong way — once qa:pass exists the tester 'post nothing and report already QA'd — skipped' unless forced, so the first green FREEZES into a permanent pass that cannot self-correct. Net effect: the gate blocks correct code over missing paperwork and passes broken code carrying correct paperwork (observed live on a bound project: main red at root validate while every label was in order). FIX (bind the pass to the artifact, do NOT add another checker): the tester records the SHA it actually validated (qa:pass + a `qa-verified: <sha>` comment), commit-gate requires that SHA to be the parent of the commit and otherwise denies with 'verified at <a>, committing on <b> — re-run /qa', and tester idempotency keys on the SHA instead of the label's existence so a later commit re-verifies automatically. Same hook, same boundary; it just stops trusting a sticker.
  - _pattern:_ a gate asserts a property of the ARTIFACT (this SHA passed), never the existence of a label — a check whose failure is cleared by relabelling is a checkpoint, not a quality control.

- **D9-session-dies-on-disconnect** · `D9` · _open_ — The fork never pulled upstream 4a8b815 (`fix: keep subagents alive across browser disconnects`) or the 01e72a6 session refactor — `git log --all` shows ui/server/core/{registry,connection}.js have NO history here. So handleClose (session.js:306-312) calls inbox.close() + abort.abort(): a backgrounded tab, a laptop sleep or a network blip ABORTS the session and kills every in-flight sub-agent, and the reconnect builds a fresh inbox that cannot drain the old queue. Upstream instead DETACHES — swappable socket, outgoing messages buffered for replay (MAX_DETACHED_BUFFER), teardown only after 75s of IDLE and never while a turn or sub-agent runs (connection.js:53-63,154,195). Surfaced 2026-08-14 while hunting the Hermes no-ack bug; it was NOT that bug's cause (that was a degraded 21h-old process) but it is a real standing defect. Decide: port registry.js + connection.js + the onSessionId/onBusyChange hooks, or accept losing in-flight work on every blip. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17: all premises hold — `git log --all` returns ZERO commits for ui/server/core/{registry,connection}.js and both files are absent; handleClose still carries both inbox.close() and abort.abort(); upstream 4a8b815 is present there. PORT SIZE now measured: registry.js + connection.js = 286 LOC upstream, plus the onSessionId/onBusyChange hooks in stream.js (our copy has neither parameter). Measurement note: count via `rtk proxy`, not `rtk … | wc -l` — the wrapper's own status line inflated this by one on the first pass.
  - _pattern:_ an upstream FIX we never pulled is a silent regression — the sync surface should track upstream fixes, not only conflicts.
